title: crescent-shift-scratch-quentin-2026-11-06
content:
Shift: Crescent (11:00 PM - 7:00 AM)
Date: 2026-11-06
Primary goal: keep latency SLOs during overnight batch + model warmup window; clear follow-ups from earlier day incidents.

Quick context notes:
- Two noisy pagers from evening: paging spike at 22:12 (user-facing 503s) and a KV-cache eviction storm at 22:47 that correlated with elevated tail latency for small token sequences.
- On-call handover: saw Slack thread with TAGS: #prod-pager; left sticky note to escalate to infra if recurrence after 0300.

Timeline (local times):
- 22:10 - Pager: 503 surge reported by synthetic checks (eu-west-1). Synthetic run id: syn-20261106-2210.
  Actions:
    - checked /monitoring/synthetics/eu-west-1 -> spike in 503s concurrent with small model rollout (v2.3.1 -> v2.4-canary).
    - rolled back canary on eu-west-1 (routing policy -> stable) 22:22.
    - immediate recovery observed; latency and error rate back to baseline by 22:25.
  Notes: suspect model variant change exposed a kernel codepath that increases memory pressure for short sequences (causing evictions). Marking as follow-up to ML infra.

- 22:40 - KV-cache eviction storm detected on cluster gpu-pool-5 (us-central). Eviction count jumped x20 in 6m. Application-level tail latency rose ~120ms.
  Actions:
    - queried metrics: node_mem_pressure, eviction_rate, kv_cache_misses.
    - sampling logs: grep for "kv_cache.*evict" in serving-runtime logs -> saw bulk flushes triggered by LRU size estimation miscalc: stack trace points to kernel selection path.
    - temporarily increased cache size threshold on pool via /ops-api (PATCH) 22:52 to buy time; thrpt stable afterwards.
  Quick commands run (for my notes):
    - kubectl -n redwood logs -l app=serving-runtime -c runtime --since=15m | grep -i "kv_cache" | head -n 50
    - curl -X PATCH https://ops.internal/api/pools/gpu-pool-5 -d '{"kv_cache_threshold": 0.8}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN"
  Notes: change is temporary; needs proper fix in kernel selector. Filed INF ticket (INF-1342) to track with applied-ml.

- 01:10 - follow-up: noticed repeated small spikes when synthetic payloads include prefix caching. Suspect prefix/KV cache interaction under quantized model variants.
  Actions:
    - took a snapshot of affected instance: /var/log/serving-runtime/evictions.log -> attached to ticket.
    - alerted Maya (applied-ml) in Slack with summary + logs.

Unresolved items to action (runbook & follow-ups):
- [ ] Runbook gap: "model-rollout-fallback" does not document rollback threshold when error_rate > 0.5% for synthetic checks. Add clear thresholds and CLI rollback playbook. Owner: Quentin. ETA: 2026-11-09. Linked: INF-2026.
- [ ] Investigate kernel selector path that mis-estimates KV size under v2.4-canary. Owner: Maya Chen (applied-ml). Add repro and unit-test. ETA: 2026-11-10. Linked: INF-1342.
- [ ] Post-incident: add a synthetic check that exercises short-sequence path for canary models (so we catch this earlier). Owner: Ramon. ETA: 2026-11-08.
- [ ] Finish temporary patch cleanup: revert PATCH that increased kv_cache_threshold once kernel fix deployed. Owner: Quentin/Ramon. Note in ops: patch id ops-patch-20261106-01.

Notes for postmortem (raw thoughts):
- Impact: brief user-facing 503s in eu-west-1 for ~12m, localized to canary region. Secondary impact: increased token latency in us-central due to cache eviction. No data loss.
- Root cause hypothesis: rollouts to v2.4 changed kernel selection heuristics for short sequences; some paths incorrectly compute LRU weight -> mass eviction.
- Immediate mitigations that helped: rollback of canary; temporary cache threshold increase; targeted instance snapshot to correlate logs.
- Longer-term mitigation: add unit tests for kernel weight estimation, add synthetic tests for short-sequence warmup, and augment rollout policy to run quick synthetic checks before promoting canary globally.

Runbook TODOs (short, actionable):
- Add section: "Canary short-sequence warmup test" with example curl payloads and pass/fail thresholds. (file: runbooks/model-deploy.md)
- Add checklist item: validate kv_cache_miss_rate < 0.5% during canary window.
- Document rollback CLI commands and ensure non-owners can execute during paging window.

Communcation / Stakeholders to ping:
- Applied ML: Maya Chen (primary), Samir Patel (backup) -> kernel selector fix.
- Platform infra: Ramon Diaz -> ops API patch review + revert coordination.
- Product: Laura Kim -> FYI on user-facing 503s for customer comms decision.

Small personal TODOs (during shift):
- [ ] tidy logs attached to INF-1342 (done: added evictions.log).
- [ ] write short blurb for handover: what changed, what to watch for next day (include synthetics id). Owner: Quentin.
- [ ] test rollback playbook in staging (dry-run) and capture commands for runbook.

Random learnings / ad-hoc notes:
- When increasing kv_cache_threshold via ops-api the change persists across restarts (ops devs pls note) -> tie patch id to ticket.
- Use synthetic ids in Slack messages to make it easy to correlate with monitoring dashboards (we already do, keep doing).

Handover summary (end of shift prep):
- Watchlist for next shift:
  * INF-1342 kernel selector fix progress (Maya)
  * ops-patch-20261106-01 revert status (Ramon)
  * Synthetic check syn-20261106-2210 results for next 24h
- Oncall notes to leave in channel: short summary + link to this doc + ticket references.

If anything flares up: prioritise rollback & region isolation (eu-west-1) over local cache tweaks. Rollback gives fastest user impact reduction.

End of notes.
summary: Nocturnal SRE scratchpad documenting 2 incidents (canary 503s and kv-cache eviction), immediate actions (rollback, temp cache increase), and concrete runbook/INF tickets for follow-up.
